rows.evidence: Q1: Sections 2.2-2.5 and 3 - authors designed a solar-pumped gravity-fed micro-tube system and measured emitter discharges on a research-farm plot. Q2: Sections 3.1-3.4 and Table 5 - measured emitter flow variation 18.96%, CUC 93.65%, Du 91.55%, stated to be within ASAE limits (qvar <20%, CUC >85%), so system qualifies on uniformity criteria. Q7: Section 4 and Section 3.5/Table 6 - from own sediment measurements authors state water should be drawn from top 3/4 of pond depth and system used only after 72 h following runoff events to avoid clogging; laminar flow must be maintained in pipe sections; design is specific to farm size. Q9: Table 5 and Sections 3.1-3.4 - CV of emitter discharge 5.40%, CD at 5% = 0.16 L/h, ranges reported for discharge (0.801-1.034 L/h), CUC across laterals (90.9-96.2%) and Du (88.3-94.6%).
rows.notes: The study measures hydraulic uniformity indices, not water savings or application efficiency directly; 'water conservation' is only implied via uniformity, so Q2 is accepted on the passage's actual content (uniformity figures). Q3: single method (field emitter discharge catch measurements); design calculations are not an independent measurement of uniformity. Q4: head losses were computed in design (Tables 3-4) and the low head loss is offered as the reason for low flow variation, but no intermediate variable linking the system to water conservation was measured, so answered no. Q5/Q6: one site, one 18 x 11 m plot. Q8: authors note the study was carried out at one location and that acreage figures are indicative, but then assert replicability; not treated as a stated limitation of the result.

notes: Full text appears complete. The technology is a gravity-fed micro-tube (star configuration) micro-irrigation system with solar pumping, which is a drip-type system; treated as matching the 'drip' technology.
